38.2. HYPERTHYROIDISM AND THYROTOXICOSIS

Fetomaternal effect of poorly controlled hyperthyroidism:

Pre – eclampsia

Still birth

Low birth weight

Alteration deficient hyperactivity

Autism

IUGR

Pre – term birth

Maternal heart failure

Fetal or neonatal Graves’ disease

(If TRAb are > 3 times of normal).

1 – 5% in uncontrolled maternal Graves’ disease

Fetal Arrhythmia, heart failure hydrops and still birth

Need FMU input

Fetal polyhydramnios because of fetal goiter

Neonatal hypothyroidism due to maternal over treatment.

These risks are directly related to severity of disease and duration of control in pregnancy.

Optimal euthyroidism by treatment and antenatal care reduce obstetric risks except placental abruption.

Pre – conceptional care:

Pre – conceptional counselling is recommended in all women with hyperthyroidism in order to minimize adverse outcome.

Discuss Adverse effects of Thyroid drugs:

Thioamides are main stay of treatment

Carbimazole CMZ – 20mg

Methimazole MMI – 15mg

Propylthiouracil PTU

Minor adverse effects 3 – 5%

Skin rash

Serious adverse effects:

Liver failure 0.1% with PTU

Agranulocytosis 0.15% with either drug

Potential teratogenic effects 2 – 4%

 

 

CMZ and MMI cause:

Embryopathy – dysmorphic features, aplasia cutis, choanal and esophageal atresia, abdominal wall defects, urinary and eye abnormalities, USD

More teratogenic effects if exposed during

6 – 10 weeks of gestation.

PTU causes

Less severe and potentially resolvable birth defects like 2 – 3% face and neck cysts

Urinary tract abnormalities.

Discontinuation of Drugs:

Discontinuation should be weighed against risk of hyperthyroidism flare in periconception period that has greatest effect on pregnancy.

 

Switching of Drug:

Switch to PTU in preference to CMZ in lowest effective dose, keep fT4 in the upper half of reference range.

Discuss effective contraception:

Avoid pregnancy in:

Active, severe disease

6 months’ post radiotherapy

6 months’ post-surgery

High level of TRAb especially if more than 3 times, as it causes fetal thyrotoxicosis

At least 2 normal range fT4 levels @ least 3 months apart.

Antenatal care:

Discontinuation of Drugs:

If women are euthyroid for > 6m0 on lower doses of anti – thyroid – CMZ < 10mg/day

PTU < 200mg/day discontinue medicine before period of teratogenicity and gestational thyrotoxicosis i-e., 6 – 10weeks.

 

Switching of drugs during pregnancy

Switch to PTU before 10weeks

Advised dose is 1:20 CMZ 10mg: PTU 200mg

No benefit of switching after 10weeks.

Switch to CMZ after 20 weeks because of risk of hepatotoxicity with PTU

Recommended dose is 20: 1 PTU 200mg to target serum fT4 @ upper half of pregnancy specific range or total T4 @ 1 – 1.5 TIMES THE UPPER LIMIT OF non – pregnant reference range to minimize risk of fetal hypothyroidism.

Monitoring of Thyroid function tests:

Stable Thyroid function

2 – 4 weeks in 1st half of pregnancy

4 – 8 weekly after 20 weeks.

Dose adjustment, switching or unstable thyroid function test – every 2 weeks.

Dose titration should target fT4. It should never be based on TSH levels that may be low and fT3 or total T3 has no role

Stopping drug on normal fT4, measure fT4 2 – 4weekly on two consecutive occasions then monitor less frequently I – e., 4 – 8weekly.

TRAb undetected or low at conception monitor TFT’s every 4 weeks until mid-trimester then 4 – 8 weeks after 20 weeks as in stable thyroid function tests

TRAb in all patients with hyperthyroidism in 1st trimester even definitive treatment has taken if positive then further monitoring @ 20 weeks and 28 weeks.

Toxic nodular goiter = more frequent monitoring as it is associated with fetal hypothyroidism due to lack of stimulation by TRAb so it is treated with lowest doses and keeping fT4 in upper limit of normal pregnancy range.

 

Fetal monitoring:

Anomaly scan if on anti – thyroid drugs – not all the anomalies are detected on USG.

Serial fetal biometry and umbilical artery Doppler @ monthly intervals from 26 – 28weeks in following patients.

Uncontrolled Graves’ dx requiring anti – thyroid drugs.

TRAb 3 times above normal level

2 – 4 weekly FHR auscultation to check fetal tachycardia if FHR > 170bpm for 10min then start surveillance earlier I – e., from 20 weeks

 

 

 

Birth:

According to obstetric indication

Fetomaternal monitoring also depends on obstetric problems.

Block and replace regimens:

Not recommended in hyperthyroidism due to increased Fetomaternal risk. Anti-thyroid cross placenta more effectively than levothyroxine and can cause fetal hypothyroidism and its sequalae.

Only indication is isolated fetal hyperthyroidism.

 

Antenatal Thyroidectomy:

Potential compromise of airway

Done in 2nd trimester

After 22 weeks’ risk of pre – term

Close peri – op monitoring of fT4 and calcium is needed to minimize risk

B – Adrenergic blocking agents like propranolol can be used temporarily to control hyperthyroid symptoms in lowest effective doses and for short duration to minimize the risk of SGA.

Neonatal Monitoring:

TFT’s @ birth and @ 1 – 2weeks after birth in following:

If mother has taken Anti – thyroid drugs during pregnancy for Graves’ dx

Ed TRAb in mother during pregnancy.

Post – Natal Care:

Autoimmunity in post – natal period is associated with

Graves’ relapse

New onset Graves’

Treatment in post – natal period

Antithyroid drugs in 2 or 3 divided doses

Both CMZ and PTU can be given

Monitoring of child’s growth who are breast feeding.

Safe maximum doses in lactation

CMZ = 20mg, PTU = 450mg daily

Transfer of CMZ in milk = 0.1 – 0.2% and PTU 0.007% - 0.077%
